newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-GRIEVING BOBEK HAS TO PICK UP THE PIECES.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-GRIEVING BOBEK HAS TO PICK UP THE PIECES.

text.p: A day after her coach Carlo Fassi died suddenly of a heart attack, Nicole Bobek must pick up the pieces at the world figure skating championships on Friday.
The 19-year-old American was distraught on Thursday as she spoke of her insistence on competing when the women's event begins on Friday - because she knew Fassi would want her to.
"From what I heard, one of Carlo's last words was to ask Christa (his wife and coaching partner) to please be with me during the competition.
"We all love him and we will miss him," she said.
Fassi, 67, died in hospital after complaining of stomach pains at the rink during the morning.
He was the coach of former Olympic women's champions Peggy Fleming and Dorothy Hamill of the United States, as well as and Britain's men's champions John Curry and Robin Cousins.
Bobek, who was third in the 1995 world championships and third at last month's U.S. Nationals, did half a practice session under Cousins' guidance on Thursday night before leaving the ice.

Cousins is expected to be at the rinkside in Fassi's place on Friday when she will face her fellow Americans -- titleholder Michelle Kwan and the new shooting star of the sport, 14-year-old Tara Lipinski.
A sweep of the medals has been widely predicted for the American trio, though Bobek's reaction to the death of her mentor could change all that.
European champion Irina Slutskaya is the likely beneficiary if any of the Americans falter.
Meanwhile, Canadian Elvis Stojko captured the men's title on Thursday with titleholder Todd Eldredge of the United States second as favourite Alexei Urmanov of Russia withdrew with a groin injury.
